$comment: The house standard, as data. This file is the single source of truth for what a repository must contain. The checker reads it, the scaffolder builds from it, the documentation is generated from it, and a test keeps the three in agreement. Where this file and the prose disagree, this file is the standard and the prose is a bug.
$version_note: Bump the version when the canonical file set or the meaning of a rule changes. A repository records the version it follows in the tag of the action it references.

root.$comment: Every file a repository carries. 'required' says whether the checker demands it. The comment is the one line that describes the file in the canonical tree.

files.comment: The front door. H1 = product name, then a pitch.
Commands, layout, traps, rails. For humans and agents alike.
Visual system. YAML frontmatter + 8 canonical sections.
Line endings, binary files, diff behaviour.
What a pull request has to say.
What happens, what was expected, how to reproduce.
The problem, the outcome, the workflow.
Blank issues off, contact links on.
The design sidecar: ramps, motion, components.
How it is put together, and why.

directories.comment: GitHub's own directory: workflows, forms, templates.
CI, release, and the house-style check.
The design sidecar and its config.
Everything executable that is not source.

readme.$comment: The four questions a reader has, in the order they ask them. A heading matches when its normalised text contains one of the keywords. The keywords cover English and Russian, because the section is the point and the wording is the project's.

product.$comment: The ten questions a product has to answer before it can be designed, built, or handed to someone else. The order is fixed: the later sections depend on the earlier ones.

design.$comment: The eight canonical sections of the DESIGN.md format. A section may be omitted; the ones that are present keep this order, because tooling parses these headers by exact name.

site.$comment: The house landing page. A repository that publishes a site carries these two files beside its index.html; a repository without a site carries neither. The path is the template's, and the files land in the directory the site already lives in.
